title: Make turn-auditor missing tool requirements target-specific
description:
Problem
The turn auditor can currently report a missing required tool by tool name only. In session-mqkis411-rlsh20, debug output effectively said lookup_rules was missing even though lookup_rules had been called. The real issue was that additional lookup_rules calls were needed for specific equipment records such as chain mail, shield, and longsword.

Tool-name-only diagnostics are too coarse for debugging and can look contradictory:
- executedToolNames includes lookup_rules
- missingRequiredTools also includes lookup_rules
- the missing target/record is only recoverable from prose repair instructions

Goal
Make auditor rejection diagnostics target-specific enough to explain what call or lookup was missing.

Acceptance Criteria
- Auditor output can distinguish missing tool calls by both tool name and target/intent, for example:
  - tool: lookup_rules, target: chain mail
  - tool: lookup_rules, target: shield
  - tool: lookup_rules, target: longsword
- Existing simple missingRequiredTools behavior may be retained for compatibility, but debug/session traces should expose the richer structure when available.
- Repair prompts should use the richer missing-call data instead of relying only on prose.
- Add tests showing that:
  1. a tool may have been executed and still be missing a specific required target
  2. auditor debug output does not misleadingly imply the tool was never called
  3. retry instruction includes the target-specific missing requirement
- Do not require perfect semantic parsing of every possible tool call target; cover the common structured cases first, especially lookup_rules and equipment/rules lookups.

Non-goals
- Do not make the auditor deterministic.
- Do not replace the current audit/retry mechanism.
- Do not block gameplay on perfect target extraction when the auditor can only provide coarse data.
close_reason: Implemented target-specific missing-call diagnostics (missingRequiredCalls) in turn auditor; PR #250
